title: fix(plugin-auth)!: an account with an enrolled second factor is signed in by no one-time code or sign-in link alone
body:
Clause-②: no (narrowing) — the one-time-code and link doors (`/phone-number/verify`, `/magic-link/verify`, and `/verify-email` when it signs the user in) answer an account with an enrolled second factor with the two-factor challenge password sign-in gives, and issue its session only after the second factor; an account with no enrolled factor signs in exactly as before.
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no published skill teaches these sign-in doors or the two-factor challenge (`git grep` over `skills/` for the three paths, `twoFactorRedirect` and `magicLink`: zero hits).

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:已开启双因素(TOTP)的账号经短信验证码、邮件登录链接、或"邮件验证后自动登录"这三扇门进入时,现在与密码登录一样先回双因素挑战,验证通过后才发会话;未开启双因素的账号完全不变。
- 为什么改:规则是"开启了双因素的账号,不能单凭一次性验证码或登录链接登录",这三扇门与密码登录对齐。
- 风险与回滚:只影响已开启双因素的账号;双因素关闭的部署零变化。Console 的短信验证码登录界面尚未读取挑战,此类账号会看到错误提示(安全方向失败);Console 的邮件验证页同样不读取挑战,链接原本会让其登录的已开启双因素账号会看到错误提示,但邮箱已验证(安全方向失败);两处界面跟进均由席位排期。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/second-factor-code-and-link-doors.ts`(门路径匹配与供应商漂移断言)、`auth-manager-plugin-list.ts` 的 twoFactor 接线(约 283 行)、`second-factor-code-and-link-doors.test.ts`。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run src/second-factor-code-and-link-doors.test.ts`,预期 41/41 通过。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

The rule: **an account with an enrolled second factor is signed in by no one-time code or sign-in link alone; a code or link door asks for the second factor, as password sign-in does.**

- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/second-factor-code-and-link-doors.ts` (new): `requireSecondFactorAtCodeAndLinkDoors(plugin)` keeps the object `twoFactor(...)` returns and appends ONE after-hook entry whose handler is the password door's own challenge handler, reused by reference (never copied), with a matcher for the fixed door paths (`/phone-number/verify`, `/magic-link/verify`, `/verify-email`) that fires whenever the door has just issued a new session the caller was not already holding. A session held for another account never stands in for the second factor, and an issued session whose token cannot be read counts as a sign-in (fail closed). So the answer is the existing challenge shape (`twoFactorRedirect` + `twoFactorMethods`, the pending two-factor cookie, no session), and TOTP, backup-code and trust-device completions behave exactly as on the password door. No new error code, no redirect marker, no query parameter.
- Fails closed on vendor drift: when the two-factor plugin exposes no after-hook whose matcher accepts `/sign-in/email`, building the auth instance throws with a message naming the module to update.
- `auth-manager-plugin-list.ts`: the `twoFactor(...)` push is wrapped in that call (plus its import).
- A door call that issues no new session is untouched: `/phone-number/verify` with `disableSession: true` or `updatePhoneNumber: true`, and `/verify-email` for a caller already holding the session it answers with.
- Docs: `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` (the SMS code example, the two-factor challenge list, the magic-link section) and `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/ARCHITECTURE.md` state the rule.
- Changeset `.changeset/plugin-auth-second-factor-code-and-link-doors.md`: `fix(plugin-auth)!:`, patch, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, with a rule-level BREAKING paragraph and its "Who moves".
- `packages/client/src/index.ts`: the TSDoc on `AuthEmailVerificationResult.status` adds one sentence: a request that would sign in an account with an enrolled second factor answers the two-factor challenge instead of the receipt. No type changes; the changeset gains `'@objectstack/client': patch`.
- `auth-manager.test.ts`: the two-factor plugin double now carries the vendor's password-challenge hook shape, since the build refuses a two-factor plugin without one.

Known and deliberate: the Console's SMS-code sign-in does not read the challenge yet, so an enrolled account sees an error there (fail-closed); its follow-up under `ui/packages/auth` is scheduled by the owning seat. The Console's verify-email page does not read the challenge either; an enrolled account that the link would have signed in sees an error there although the address is verified (fail-closed), same follow-up. Magic link has no Console consumer.

## Tests

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/second-factor-code-and-link-doors.test.ts`, 41 cases, real `AuthManager.handleRequest` over the real better-auth pipeline; codes and links are the ones the running plugins handed to the SMS and email services; every credential question is asked at `GET /get-session`.

Per door (`/phone-number/verify`, `/magic-link/verify`, `/verify-email` with auto sign-in):
- an enrolled account gets the challenge and no usable credential: the response cookie, the `set-auth-token` header and any body `token` each resolve to nobody, and the account's session-row count is unchanged;
- completing TOTP after the challenge yields the session;
- a backup code also completes it;
- a valid trust-device cookie skips the challenge and is rotated, as on the password door;
- a session held for another account does not stand in for the second factor: the enrolled account's door call carries another account's live session, once as a cookie and once as `Authorization: Bearer`, and still gets the challenge, no usable credential and an unchanged row count;
- CONTROL: an account with no enrolled factor is signed in as before (cookie and bearer both resolve, one new session row).

The address-change link on `/verify-email`, for both the legacy token and the `change-email-verification` token type: with no session an enrolled account gets the challenge and no usable credential; signed in as the same account it is not challenged, keeps its session, and the address changes.

Also: magic link and verify-email on the `callbackURL` redirect lane give an enrolled account no session (plus a magic-link redirect-lane CONTROL); `updatePhoneNumber: true` for a signed-in enrolled account is not challenged and keeps its session; `disableSession: true` issues no session and no challenge; verify-email for an enrolled account already signed in keeps that session; CONTROL: password sign-in by email and by phone still challenge an enrolled account and sign a plain one in; the composition builds with two-factor off and phone on; the extension appends exactly one entry reusing the password challenge handler by reference; the vendor-drift assertion throws when the hook is absent; the door matcher's readings, including the fail-closed pin (an issued session whose token cannot be read counts as a sign-in).

## Acceptance notes

- Ablation on `1dae135805` (each mutation through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, landing proven on disk, restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty; the suite imports the module from `src/`, so no build sits between mutation and run):
  - remove `/phone-number/verify` from the door list: 6 red (challenge, TOTP, backup code, trust-device, foreign session as cookie and as bearer), 35 green;
  - remove `/magic-link/verify`: 7 red (those six plus the redirect lane), 34 green;
  - remove `/verify-email`: 9 red (those six, the redirect lane, and both address-change tokens with no session), 32 green;
  - remove the drift assertion's throw: 1 red (the drift case), 40 green;
  - drop the "caller already holds this session" condition: 4 red (both address-change tokens while signed in, verify-email while signed in, the matcher case), 37 green;
  - revert the fail-closed reading of an unreadable token: 1 red (the fail-closed pin), 40 green;
  - let any held session exempt the door: 7 red (the foreign-session pins at all three doors, both carriers, plus a matcher case), 34 green.
- The file surface grew by one test double in `auth-manager.test.ts` (plugin-registration describe), owed by the fail-closed assertion.
